You want to dive into the weeds of T1195.002, huh? Alright, let me grab a cup of coffee and walk you through this one.

T1195.002, also known as "Abuse of Software Supply Chain," is a technique used by threat actors to compromise a software supply chain by exploiting vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies or libraries used by a larger application. This technique can lead to remote code execution, denial-of-service (DoS), or other types of attacks.

On our Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server, running kernel 5.15.0-91, I can give you an example of how this might play out. Suppose we're running an application that uses a popular JavaScript library, let's call it "lib-jquery". If lib-jquery has a known vulnerability (think a buffer overflow or a privilege escalation bug), an attacker could exploit it to gain access to our system.
